column1: agriculture (the art or science of cultivating the ground)
blood (vital liquid flowing in human and animal bodies)
eagle (any of several large carnivorous birds in the family Accipitridae)
egg (approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, insects, reptiles, and other animals, housing the embryo within a membrane or shell during its development)
feather (branching, hair-like structure that grows on the bodies of birds)
fingernail (covering near the tip of finger)
grow ((transitive) to cause something to become bigger)
hair (pigmented filament of keratin on the skin of humans and other mammals)
health (state of being free of physical or psychological disease, illness, or malfunction)
horn (growth on the heads of certain animals)
human (of or belonging to the species Homo sapiens)
jacket (piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse)
louse (an insect of the order Psocodea)
money (means of exchange and measure of value)
mother (female (human) who gives birth to or parents a child)
mouth (the opening of a creature through which food is ingested — see also lip, face)
peanut butter (spread made from ground peanuts)
school (an institution dedicated to teaching and learning)
sibling (person who shares same parents — see also brother, sister)
skin (outer protective layer of the body of a person or animal)
speak (to communicate with one's voice using words)
stop (not to continue — see also cease, desist)
swap (exchange or give (something) in exchange for)
tail (appendage of an animal — see also dock)
